subject: Production: quota flapping -> 429/retry storm (MedTrix)
messages:
From: Jill Ramos <jill.ramos@medtrix.health>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: URGENT: Production 429 spike + timeouts (started ~09:00 PST)

Hi Ben / Vivek,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 429 responses and downstream timeouts at ~09:00 PST. Error rate has climbed to ~18-22% across our production endpoints (primarily /v1/generate and /v1/chat). User-facing sessions are timing out; retries from our side are making things worse (we've had two automated retry waves). Traffic pattern hasn’t changed on our side — same QPS and burst profile as usual.

Attached: medtrix_500-429-logs.zip (sample 429/500 traces + client retry headers).

This is impacting our critical workflows. Please advise immediate mitigation and ETA. We need an exec-level contact.

Thanks,
Jill Ramos
Director of Engineering
MedTrix Health

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:28:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: URGENT: Production 429 spike + timeouts (started ~09:00 PST)

Looping in CS and oncall eng. Short summary: MedTrix seeing 20% 429s and retry amplification. Requesting immediate mitigation and a runbook we can execute with them. Proposed immediate steps:
- Apply temporary quota bump for MedTrix org (10x) for 1 hour
- Enable fallback to smaller model variant for high-latency calls
- Ask MedTrix to add exponential backoff + jitter client-side for 60min
- Engineering: triage and identify root cause (mapping/routing/config).

I attached the quick mitigation runbook. Naomi — can you take the lead on triage and a rollback if needed? Vivek — fine to escalate to ops execs if this affects SLAs. Monica — can you be primary customer contact?

Attachments: mitigation_runbook.pdf

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Fwd: URGENT: Production 429 spike + timeouts (started ~09:00 PST)

On Fri, Nov 27, 2026 at 09:28 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Looping in CS and oncall eng...

Quick triage update (initial):
- Timeline: config rollout at 08:56 PST engaged a label-swap between project labels "mtx-prod-a" and "mtx-prod-b".
- Root cause (prelim): a mapping rule in the quota service (project->org tier) was inverted for two projects due to a deployment bug in the tiering controller. Those projects were assigned the low-throughput tier which caused immediate 429s under normal traffic.
- Observable: sudden jump in per-project rate-limiter rejects starting 08:59, KV cache misses on routing table, and a correlated increase in retries from the client (retry headers show immediate retry w/o jitter).

Actions taken (09:30-09:40):
1) Rolled back the tiering controller change to the previous commit (08:55 version).
2) Manually reassigned the two affected projects to the correct tier mapping (re-warmed routing caches).
3) Applied a temporary org-level quota bump for MedTrix (10x) as short-term relief.
4) Disabled strict per-project burst enforcement for 15 minutes to allow catch-up.
5) Disabled an aggressive client-stuck requeue path that was amplifying retries.

Immediate ask from MedTrix: can they apply client-side jitter/backoff? Yes — recommend exponential backoff with full jitter and 60s max.

Next: we will monitor (metrics + traces) for 60 minutes and confirm 429s drop. If behavior persists, plan is to re-run rollback and consider rolling back the tiering controller across the entire region.

Will post updated timeline as we see metrics.

-naomi
Naomi Feldman
SRE, Redwood Inference (oncall)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Jill Ramos <jill.ramos@medtrix.health>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 10:10:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: URGENT: Production 429 spike + timeouts (started ~09:00 PST)

Jill — first, apologies for the disruption. Quick update and next steps from our side: 

What we did (live):
- Rolled back the tiering controller change that introduced inverted project->tier mapping.
- Manually reassigned the two impacted projects to their correct tiers and re-warmed caches.
- Applied a temporary org quota uplift (10x) for MedTrix to remove immediate pressure while we validate.
- Disabled per-project burst enforcement for 15m and turned off an internal retry requeue path that was amplifying failures.

What we need from MedTrix (recommended, immediate):
- Add exponential backoff with full jitter for retries (initial backoff 200ms, max 60s) for 60 minutes. This will reduce client-side retry amplification while we observe.
- Share any remaining large bulk jobs that could be paused for 30 minutes (helps stabilize queues).

Monitoring & follow up:
- Naomi and Rishi are monitoring metrics and will confirm when 429s are down to normal (<1%).
- We propose a 2-hour check-in at 12:00 PST to review post-condition and next steps.

We will provide a written incident summary and proposed changes to prevent re-occurrence (improved rollout validation for tiering controller, additional canary checks, automated rollback triggers).

Again — very sorry for the impact. Ben / Monica will coordinate procurement / SLA credit conversations.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

From: Jill Ramos <jill.ramos@medtrix.health>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 12:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: Production 429 spike + timeouts (started ~09:00 PST)

Thanks for the fast action. Traffic returned to normal (~0.7% 429) after ~30 minutes from the rollback and temporary bump. We implemented client-side jitter per your guidance and have paused a non-critical batch job for 45 minutes.

Immediate asks from MedTrix: 
- Please share the incident postmortem and a prevention plan (we need an assurance that tiering rollouts will not cause production flaps).
- Our procurement team will open an SLA credit request — looping them in (procurement@medtrix.health).

We appreciate the quick collaboration; we’ll expect the postmortem and proposed safeguards.

-Jill
Director of Engineering
MedTrix Health
